name: flowchart
renderNote: Shapes, line labels, group titles and notes are authored as a list and emitted as an HTML measuring harness; the browser pass measures it in the deck's own fonts, lays the chart out with the shared elbow router and paints every mark into the `<svg>`. Once painted the harness leaves layout, so a drawn slide is SVG in practice; it is hybrid because the harness is what shows until the pass runs, or where it cannot.

projection.frame: each box is a thing and each line says how one thing leads to or depends on another

description: A free-form flowchart: shapes, groups and lines, written as a list.
purpose: Use for a process or decision flow, an org chart, a data flow or a system map: any set of boxes where the lines between them are the point. Every list item is a shape; a sub-list of shapes makes its parent a group; an arrow in a row connects shapes by name. Nothing implies order, so the same grammar draws a tree, a pipeline or a few disconnected boxes.

title.description: Slide heading: name the takeaway, not the diagram.

eyebrow.description: Optional eyebrow naming the system or domain.

shapes.description: One item per shape, in any order. The shape's name is its displayed text; other rows refer to it by that name, ignoring case. A trailing inline-code span styles it: an outline (`:box` `:square` `:pill` `:diamond` `:circle` `:cylinder` `:io` `:doc`), a slot `:c1`…`:c8`, one channel `:fill-cN` / `:border-cN` / `:text-cN`, a status word (`done`, `fail`, …) or an id `#kyc` to refer to it by.

groups.description: A sub-list of shapes makes its parent item a GROUP, drawn as a tinted background behind its members, like a Mermaid subgraph. `:cN` on a group tints it. Groups nest. A line can start or end at a group.

connections.description: An arrow in a row connects shapes: `A -> B`, `A => B` (the heavy main path), `A -- B` (no head), `A <-> B`, `A <- B`. A label sits inside the arrow: `-ships via->`. A row may start with the arrow (`- => B`), meaning "from the item this row sits under", or name its source (`- A => B`). `&` fans out: `A -> B & C`. A trailing span after the target styles the line: `:dashed` `:dotted` `:open` `:dot` `:cross` `:loose` `:cN`.

notes.description: A `>` blockquote under a shape is a note pinned to it, drawn as a card on a dotted tether.

key.description: The chart derives its own key from what it uses. One bracketed span right below the list renames entries by the word you typed: `` `[{=>, Happy path}, {:dotted, Later}]` ``. It only renames; it never hides or adds an entry.

caption.description: An italic paragraph below becomes the chart caption.

skeleton:
<!-- _class: flowchart -->

## The flow in one line.

- Start `:pill` => Check => Decide?
- Decide? `:diamond`
  - -yes-> Ship
  - -no-> Fix -> Check

whenToUse.title: The lines are the point
whenToUse.body: A flowchart earns its space when the audience needs to see what connects to what: a decision flow, who reports to whom, where data goes. If the boxes are the point and the order is fixed, a step list or timeline reads faster.

whenToUse.title: Up to about a dozen shapes
whenToUse.body: Starting budgets: a decision flow six steps deep with four branches; an org chart three levels deep and eight across; a data flow three groups and twelve shapes; a system map ten shapes. Past that the type shrinks toward the floor; split into an overview and detail slides.

whenToUse.title: Free-form, not a state machine
whenToUse.body: For a machine with states and events, where the numbering is the reference, use `state-chart`. A flowchart implies no order and has no start or end markers.

antiPatterns.title: A sequence dressed as a flowchart
antiPatterns.body: Five boxes in a line with arrows between them is a list with decoration. Use `list-steps` or `timeline-list`, which read faster and fit more words.

antiPatterns.title: Timed interactions or schedules
antiPatterns.body: Messages between actors over time are a sequence diagram (`diagram` with Mermaid); work across dates is `gantt` or `roadmap`.

antiPatterns.title: Color with no key
antiPatterns.body: Every slot and status the chart uses shows up in the derived key. Renaming entries is free; painting meaning the reader cannot decode is not.

related.name: state-chart
related.when: a finite-state machine: numbered states, events between them, a start and an end

related.name: diagram
related.when: you need Mermaid's full grammar: sequence, class or entity diagrams, or a flowchart with subgraph directions and styles this grammar does not cover

related.name: list-steps
related.when: a linear procedure with no branching and no lines worth drawing

related.name: roadmap
related.when: parallel workstreams across phases, where time is the axis

commonMistakes.mistake: Nesting a shape under a connection row.
commonMistakes.fix: A sub-list makes its parent a GROUP, so it must sit under a shape's row, never under `- -> B`. Lint names it: flowchart-nested-under-connection.

commonMistakes.mistake: Styling a shape from the line that points at it (`-> B `:diamond``).
commonMistakes.fix: A span after a connection's target styles the LINE. Give B its own row and put `:diamond` there.

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing an arrow that is meant as text (`Input -> Output` as one name).
commonMistakes.fix: Escape it: `Input \-> Output`. A comparison like `2 => 3` is warned about for the same reason.

variantDecisionRule.useWhen: Almost always. The chart lays itself out both ways and keeps whichever sets the type larger on the stage. A dense chart whose type nears the floor takes the universal `compact` modifier, which tightens the spacing.
The flow must read left to right whatever the stage shape (a pipeline, a data flow). On a portrait deck `lr` falls back to `tb`, because a row cannot fit a tall box.
The flow must read top to bottom (an org chart, a decision tree).

lr.label: Left-to-right
lr.summary: Pins the flow left to right.
lr.sample:
<!-- _class: flowchart lr -->

## Events land in the warehouse within a minute.

- Web events `:io` => Ingest queue => Stream processor => Warehouse
- Warehouse `:cylinder`
  - -> BI dashboards
  - -nightly-> ML training
- BI dashboards `:doc`

tb.label: Top-to-bottom
tb.summary: Pins the flow top to bottom.
tb.sample:
<!-- _class: flowchart tb -->

## The operating model has three lines of reporting.

- Chief executive `:c1`
  - -- Finance & Technology & Operations
- Finance
  - -- Controller & Planning
- Technology
  - -- Platform & Security

handles.note: A harness tile holds its name span and nothing else.
A key entry is a swatch plus its label.

pane.noBudget: a flowchart scales to its box, and its list mixes shapes with connection rows, so a count of list items is not its size
